merger_name: Francisco Partners – Majority interest in Command Alkon

anzsic_codes.name: Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services
Computer System Design and Related Services

merger_description:
Pursuant to a unit purchase agreement, funds advised by Francisco Partners Management, L.P. (together with its affiliated funds, **Francisco Partners**) will indirectly acquire all the equity interests in Project Potter Holdings, LLC, together with its subsidiaries, including Command Alkon Australia Pty Ltd (**Command Alkon**), that are currently held by funds managed by Thoma Bravo LP (**Thoma Bravo**) and certain other equity holders (the **Acquisition**).

Command Alkon is currently jointly controlled by Thoma Bravo and Heidelberg Materials AG (**Heidelberg Materials**).

Following completion of the Acquisition, Francisco Partners and Heidelberg Materials will jointly control Command Alkon.

Francisco Partners is a global investment firm headquartered in San Francisco. It is a technology-focused investment firm with significant experience investing in and supporting technology companies.

Command Alkon is headquartered in Ohio and consists of several software companies that deliver automation software solutions. These solutions are used in the heavy building materials industry for purposes including pricing and quoting, order taking, scheduling and delivery, dispatching, batching, ticketing, truck tracking and management, and quality control, in connection with the production of materials such as ready-mixed or pre-cast concrete, cement, aggregates and asphalt.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given there is no horizontal or vertical
overlap between Francisco Partners (or its connected entities) and
Command Alkon in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
